office_does: The County Clerk keeps the official records of Superior Court cases and decisions and runs the office where the public files court matters such as protection orders and family-law cases.
race_blurb: Open seat after a county budget cut closed the Clerk's Office public counter for months; limited in-person service resumed September 21. Nicole Miller, a former county Racial Equity Program Manager running on leadership experience, narrowly led Garrett Cady, an independent Clerk's Office employee endorsed by the outgoing clerk, 50.7% to 48.7% in the primary.

candidates.summary: Child-welfare consultant and former Thurston County Racial Equity Program Manager with about 30 years in public service, running from outside the Clerk's Office on leadership and restoring full public access.
highlights: Pledges reliable, full-time in-person access, saying "part-time access is not enough" [S2][S4]
Would take part fully in county budget meetings so "there should be no surprises," and look for ways to increase revenue and reduce costs [S5]
Argues the Clerk is an elected executive and that knowing existing procedures differs from leading an organization [S2][S6]
Endorsed by three county commissioners and the 22nd LD's state senator and representatives [S2]
Narrowly led the certified August primary with 50.72% [S8]

experience.basis: Comes from outside the Clerk's Office and runs on changing how it serves the public, drawing on long public-service management experience rather than office tenure.

spending.basis: Pairs a pledge to restore full-time counter service with examining ways to increase revenue and reduce costs.

candidates.summary: Clerk's Office proceedings specialist and former juvenile court assistant from Yelm, running as an independent with the backing of the outgoing clerk, office leadership and 21 other county clerks.
highlights: Current Clerk's Office employee who has worked the front counter and as a courtroom clerk and trains newer staff [S1][S2]
Calls the commissioners' 2026-2027 budget cut to the office "disproportionate" and pledges to keep all in-person services [S2]
Would restore and expand the Domestic Violence Liaison Program [S1][S2]
Runs as an independent, saying "there is absolutely no place for politics in the Clerk's Office" [S2]
Endorsed by Clerk Linda Myhre Enlow and 21 other county clerks [S2]

experience.basis: Continuity candidate: works inside the Clerk's Office and is endorsed by the outgoing clerk, chief deputy and office staff; no elected record.

reform.basis: Runs as an independent and repeatedly says the clerk must be free of political influence, like nonpartisan judges; no wider structural-reform agenda.

spending.basis: Criticizes the budget cut to the office as disproportionate and pledges to restore and enhance in-person and domestic-violence services.
